$comment: Canonical acceptance-verdict corpus (#2512, E48.78). The acceptance verdict wire shape is validated by TWO hand-maintained twins that cannot import each other: validateAcceptanceVerdict in package main of runner/cmd/fishhawk-runner (the runner module does not require the backend module) and acceptanceBody.validate in backend/internal/server. This file is the shared proof surface: each side runs the SAME rows and must produce the SAME admit/reject partition. The claim is CORPUS AGREEMENT, not byte-carrying -- no test carries bytes returned by one validator into the other, which is unimplementable across the module boundary. Mirrored verbatim into both testdata dirs by scripts/sync-schemas; CI's schema-sync gate red-lines any divergence between the three copies. Named *-fixtures.json (NOT *.schema.json) so the docs/spec/*.schema.json sync loop never globs it.

rows.name: passed-no-criteria
rows.reason: The pre-existing minimal shape: a settled pass with no itemized evidence.

rows.name: passed-with-passed-row
rows.reason: The ordinary happy path.

rows.name: failed-with-failure-mode
rows.reason: A real defect. failure_mode is required on a failed verdict.

rows.name: undecidable-row-valid

criteria.undecidable_reason: the preview exposes no seam that distinguishes the two outcomes

rows.reason: The new per-criterion value with a non-empty reason. The top-level verdict stays passed -- the server derives the undecidable disposition from the rows.

rows.name: undecidable-row-reason-absent
rows.reason: undecidable_reason is REQUIRED on an undecidable row: without it the row is indistinguishable from a silently dropped criterion.

rows.name: undecidable-row-reason-empty
rows.reason: An empty reason carries no information.

rows.name: undecidable-row-reason-whitespace-only
rows.reason: THE NAMED TWIN-DIVERGENCE RISK: a whitespace-only reason is the shape one validator would admit and the other reject if either side compared against the empty string instead of trimming. A divergence here strands a completed acceptance stage while both suites stay green.

rows.name: undecidable-reason-on-passed-row-non-empty
rows.reason: The field belongs ONLY on an undecidable row.

rows.name: undecidable-reason-on-passed-row-empty
rows.reason: BINDING CONDITION 1: rejected on PRESENCE, not on emptiness. A validator that decodes the field into a plain string cannot tell this row from the absent-field row and would silently admit it.

rows.name: undecidable-reason-on-failed-row-empty
rows.reason: Same presence rule on a failed row.

rows.name: undecidable-reason-on-skipped-row-non-empty
rows.reason: Same presence rule on a skipped row. skipped and undecidable are distinct dispositions.

rows.name: passed-row-reason-absent-accepted
rows.reason: The absent-field control that pairs with the two rejection rows above: absence is admitted, presence is not.

rows.name: top-level-verdict-undecidable
rows.reason: undecidable is SERVER-DERIVED and unforgeable: the top-level wire enum stays passed|failed on BOTH validators, so a producer cannot ship it. Both twins reject.

rows.name: undecidable-row-unknown-field
rows.reason: DisallowUnknownFields does not descend into a json.RawMessage field, so the strict decode is re-applied per criteria element. A typo'd field name must fail closed rather than be silently dropped.

rows.name: top-level-unknown-field
rows.reason: The TOP-LEVEL strict decode, the sibling of the per-element one above. undecidable_reason is a per-criterion field; hoisted to the top level it is an unknown field and must fail closed on both twins. Without this row the corpus cannot detect a refactor that drops top-level DisallowUnknownFields on either side.

rows.name: mixed-failed-and-undecidable
rows.reason: Both values coexist on one verdict. The server's precedence ladder puts failed strictly above undecidable.

rows.name: all-undecidable
rows.reason: The nothing-was-verified arm: a valid wire body the server records as undecidable, never as a pass.

rows.name: unknown-criterion-result
rows.reason: The result enum is closed. undecidable did not open it to arbitrary values.

rows.name: criteria-object-keyed-coercion
rows.reason: The pre-existing #1574 object-keyed coercion, exercised WITH an undecidable row so the new field survives the coercion path on both sides.

rows.name: criteria-object-keyed-bad-undecidable
rows.reason: The reason requirement applies after coercion too -- the object-keyed path must not bypass it.

rows.name: target-url-schemeless-coercion
rows.reason: The pre-existing schemeless target_url coercion, pinned here so the corpus also covers the existing twin rules.

rows.name: target-url-foreign-scheme
rows.reason: A foreign scheme fails closed on both sides.

rows.name: failed-missing-failure-mode
rows.reason: Pre-existing rule, kept in the corpus so a refactor of the per-criterion switch cannot quietly loosen the verdict switch beside it.

rows.name: criterion-missing-id
rows.reason: id is the plan-criterion join key and is required on every row, undecidable included.
